display.purpose: Characters title and current character name; New character uses clamp(28px, 2.3vw, 40px) and 28px on phones.

headline.purpose: Selected character name below the Characters stage: 30px default, 38px above 1100px wide and 541px tall, 28px in the phone layout, 24px in short landscape.

title.purpose: Equipment panel headings (19px). Standard dialog headings are 18px; Your characters is 24px.

body.purpose: Tabs, item names and form text in panels; the app default text is 14px/1.4 (Bronze base.css is not loaded).

action.purpose: Labels of bronze-filled scene primary actions (14px in the phone layout).

label.purpose: Header actions, small descriptions, counts and eyebrows.

caption.purpose: Help hints, field sub-labels, costs and keyboard hints.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Menus, popovers, tooltips, toasts and the playback bar, with a --bu-blur (12px) backdrop blur on floating surfaces.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Modal dialogs over a black scrim at 50% (34% in light).

motion.name: duration
motion.purpose: Bronze state transitions; 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion, where PixelDoll also removes CSS transitions and animations (sprite playback is unaffected).

motion.name: blur
motion.purpose: Backdrop blur on floating surfaces; removed for reduced transparency or more contrast.

layout.edge: clamp(28px, 2.92vw, 56px) on wide desktop; 24px with a fixed 300px rail up to 1100px wide; 20px in the phone layout

layout.viewTabs: top center from 1280px wide; in the character details from 761px to 1279px wide; both only when at least 541px tall
layout.equipmentGrid: desktop two columns, 16px gaps, full-width None; phones three columns, 8px gaps, None as a cell
layout.creator: four columns, three at 1250px, two at 1000px, stacked on phones

narrative.northStar: In character views, the character is prominent and controls are grouped around it.
narrative.overview:
Characters and Customize share a full-window world background: a photographic floor that fades into mist (dark stone in dark mode, pale polished stone in light mode). Characters centers the selected character beside the library. Customize places the character's name and description at the upper left, equipment and colors in a column on the right, and the playback controls in a small floating bar under the character. New character instead uses a full-screen form over the same world background. On phones the pieces stack: header, name, view tabs, a shorter stage, and an expandable bottom panel for equipment.

The look is calm and modern: system sans-serif text, Lucide line icons, thin borders, and a single warm bronze accent. The only serif is Georgia for screen titles and character names. The character's pixels are never lit, tinted, filtered or resized with smoothing. Internally the two world themes are called Obsidian (dark) and Porcelain (light), together "Obsidian / Porcelain Bronze" ([approved direction](docs/design/2026-10-22-redesign/round-4-discussion/current-design.md)).

Density is low around the stage and moderate in the right column, where people do most of their work: picking items, recoloring and adding new items.
keyCharacteristics: Full-window world background with the character as the visual focus of character views.
Dark by default, with a complete light theme (not an inverted filter).
One accent color, bronze, used for selection, focus, links and primary actions.
Georgia only for titles and names; Segoe UI / system sans-serif for everything else.
Controls mostly sit straight on the scene as text and icons; borders appear where you choose something.
Native dialogs and menus with Bronze styling; bottom sheets on phones.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Bronze marks selection, focus, links and primary actions. Ordinary headings and body copy stay neutral. Some recovery and item-review states show more than one bronze-filled action.

rules.name: The Untouched Sprite Rule
rules.body: UI colors never reach the character. No lighting, tint, glow, shadow or color grading is applied to actor pixels; palette changes happen only through the user's own recoloring.

rules.name: The User Color Rule
rules.body: Palette swatches show the user's data, not the theme. A selected palette ramp gets a text-colored outline (2px, offset 2px), not a bronze one, so it stays visible against any ramp.

rules.name: The Names Are Serif Rule
rules.body: Georgia is only for screen titles and character names. Buttons, tabs, labels and data are always sans-serif.

rules.name: The No Pixel Type Rule
rules.body: Interface typography and functional icons are never pixel fonts or pixel icons; character and equipment artwork remain pixel art (PLAN.md D9).

rules.name: The Flat Scene Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the scene gets a shadow except floating layers. With reduced transparency or more contrast, translucent materials become solid surface and blur is removed. In forced-colors mode, semantic UI roles switch to system colors; artwork and user color data are separate from those roles.

dos: **Do** take every color, border, radius, shadow and state from Bronze tokens; fix shared appearance in `@shilo/bronze-ui`, release it, then update the dependency.
**Do** keep the character's visual prominence and the existing reading gradients on character views.
**Do** use bronze for selection, focus, links and primary actions.
**Do** use Georgia only for screen titles and character names, and Lucide for functional icons at the size their component sets.
**Do** keep primary touch targets about 44px and inputs at 16px or larger on phones.
**Do** check every visual change in dark and light at desktop and phone sizes (including 320×568 and 844×390).
donts: **Don't** light, tint, filter, shadow or smoothly scale character or equipment pixels.
**Don't** use pixel fonts, pixel icons or pixel-style borders for interface text and controls.
**Don't** add a second palette, local color overrides or new theme dependencies in PixelDoll.
**Don't** add decorative glows, gradients or glass effects in routine work; keep the existing Bronze materials, reading gradients and phone sheet treatment.
**Don't** put boxes and shadows around panels that sit on the scene, or add unrelated scenery or props to the world.
**Don't** use bronze for ordinary headings, body copy or decoration.
